events.title: UNGA 81: Trump address and whirlwind bilaterals
events.why_it_matters: Trump speaks opening day (~9:55 a.m. ET) defending the Iran war and UNGA diplomacy while meeting Zelensky, Takaichi, Burnham and GCC leaders, so Hormuz, diesel and tariff rhetoric can reprice before Xi arrives.
events.what_to_watch: Any Hormuz-access, Iran-nuclear, or secondary-tariff language versus a softer energy-truce pitch.

events.title: Trump–Zelensky UNGA sideline on energy-infrastructure truce
events.why_it_matters: A reciprocal halt on energy-infrastructure strikes is the live diesel/refining story: Trump wants Ukraine to stop hitting Russian refineries into midterms; Zelensky wants verifiable Russian restraint before winter.
events.what_to_watch: Whether a written or even verbal reciprocal pause is announced, and any Russian response via Lavrov.

events.title: Hormuz tanker war still live; Brent ~$101–102
events.why_it_matters: Visible Hormuz transits remain a trickle versus pre-war norms after the Sept 17–18 IRGC strike on Togo-flagged tanker Trend; Brent near $101.5 is a war premium feeding G3 inflation and the Warsh hike path.
events.what_to_watch: Daily transit counts, war-risk premia, any UNGA Iran de-escalation, and whether Brent holds above $100 into the Xi visit.

events.title: Trump–Xi Washington summit (Xi visit Sept 23–25)
events.why_it_matters: Highest-stakes US–China event of the quarter: possible ~$30bn '30-by-30' tariff cuts and Busan-truce extension versus Taiwan arms, rare earths, AI guardrails, and the newly signed Graham secondary-tariff law.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the Nov 10 Busan truce is extended, any $14bn Taiwan arms pause/approval, and whether secondary tariffs on Chinese Russian-oil purchases are waived or brandished.

events.title: Pezeshkian UNGA address; possible Trump–Iran sideline
events.why_it_matters: Iranian President Pezeshkian speaks Sept 23; Trump has said he is 'probably open' to a bilateral amid the Hormuz tanker war, so even a non-meeting is an oil-vol event.
events.what_to_watch: Confirmed bilateral or hard no; any language on Hormuz corridors versus more IRGC enforcement.

events.title: US Section 338 import bans on selected Canadian goods
events.why_it_matters: Sept 8 proclamations convert parts of the 50% Canada tit-for-tat into outright bans on specified beer/wine/spirits, some dairy/whey, and large motorcycles at 12:01 a.m. ET Sept 29.
events.what_to_watch: Last-minute scope carve-outs, Canadian retaliation, and whether USMCA goods stay inside the ban.

events.title: August PCE / personal income (plus Q2 GDP third estimate)
events.why_it_matters: First post-Warsh inflation print: consensus clusters around core PCE +0.25–0.28% m/m and ~3.3% y/y, with NIPA annual-update revisions that could shave y/y by 0.1–0.2pp and reprice the extra 2026 hike in the SEP.
events.what_to_watch: Core PCE m/m versus 0.25%, services ex-housing, and whether revisions lower the y/y level the FOMC just marked up to 3.4–3.7%.

events.title: September employment report (NFP)
events.why_it_matters: Last labor print before the Oct 27–28 FOMC; consensus ~+120k payrolls and 4.3% unemployment will decide whether the Warsh majority's extra 25bp by year-end stays priced.
events.what_to_watch: Payrolls vs +120k, unemployment vs 4.3%, average hourly earnings, and revisions to prior months.

events.title: August JOLTS job openings
events.why_it_matters: Opens the labor week into NFP; consensus ~7.2 million openings after July's 7.27 million, a gauge of how much tightness the Warsh Fed still sees.
events.what_to_watch: Openings vs ~7.2m, quits rate, and any further cooling in professional/business openings.

events.title: Costco Q4 FY2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Largest S&P 500 print this week and a high-frequency read on US consumer traffic/mix with gasoline and food inflation still sticky from Hormuz.
events.what_to_watch: Comparable sales ex-gas, membership-fee commentary, and any guidance that confirms or breaks the August retail-sales rebound.

events.title: Micron fiscal Q4 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Only mega-semiconductor bellwether in this window; HBM/AI memory demand versus China export-control and Trump–Xi AI-guardrail risk.
events.what_to_watch: HBM pricing/volume, data-center mix, and any commentary on China or export licenses around the summit.

events.title: Accenture FY2026 Q4 earnings
events.why_it_matters: IT-services/AI-spending bellwether for enterprise capex after G3 tightening; bookings will show whether AI projects are still funded into a higher-for-longer Warsh path.
events.what_to_watch: New bookings, generative-AI commentary, and FY2027 guidance versus a still-hawkish SEP.

events.title: Nike Q1 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Global consumer/China-demand read one week after Trump–Xi; consensus ~$0.44–0.45 EPS and ~$11.35bn sales.
events.what_to_watch: Greater China sales, inventory, and any tariff/wholesale commentary after the summit.

events.title: SpaceX (SPCX) Day-105 lockup tranche ~328m shares
events.why_it_matters: Fourth staggered post-IPO unlock (~7% of the 180-day block) lands the same day as Trump–Xi and Costco, adding supply into a still-thin mega-IPO float.
events.what_to_watch: Actual selling versus eligibility, and whether the Oct 9/Oct 24 tranches get pulled forward in positioning.

events.title: Bamboo Insurance (~$665m) and Amaero IPOs
events.why_it_matters: Largest near-term US listing this week (Bamboo ~$665m) is a risk-appetite test while mega-cap earnings are dark; Amaero is a smaller industrial add-on.
events.what_to_watch: Pricing versus range and first-day pop/dump as a read on IPO window health.

events.title: China NBS and Caixin September PMIs
events.why_it_matters: First China activity pulse after the Trump–Xi meeting; August NBS manufacturing was still 49.8 while exports/high-tech ran hot — a miss would expose the domestic-demand hole Xi brings to Washington.
events.what_to_watch: NBS manufacturing back above 50 or not, new-export orders, and Caixin vs official divergence.

events.title: OPEC+7 production meeting for November quotas
events.why_it_matters: Sept 6 virtual meeting held October output flat at ~31.01 mb/d after completing the 1.65 mb/d voluntary-cut rollback; Hormuz-constrained actual barrels still sit below quotas.
events.what_to_watch: Hold vs another small hike, compensation for overproducers, and any Saudi language on $100 oil as a war premium.

events.title: Google ad-tech joint proposed final judgment due
events.why_it_matters: Parties must file a joint (or competing) final judgment after Judge Brinkema rejected an AdX breakup and imposed six-year behavioral remedies plus a monitor.
events.what_to_watch: Disputed provisions on AdX/DFP interoperability, worldwide scope, and whether Google signals an appeal.

events.title: BoJ 1.25% policy rate becomes effective
events.why_it_matters: The Sept 18 7–2 hike to a 31-year high actually hits money markets the same day as Trump–Xi, the classic yen-carry unwind date with oil imports already stressing Japan's trade balance.
events.what_to_watch: USD/JPY, Japanese bank shares, and whether Takaichi's UNGA comments lean against further hikes.

events.title: August new-home sales
events.why_it_matters: Housing is already cracking (existing sales 3.98m, 4.9 months' supply) even as nominal retail sales rebounded; July new-home sales slumped to 607k SAAR.
events.what_to_watch: Whether August new-home sales stabilize after the 10.5% July drop, and any further builder incentives.

events.title: ECB Monetary Policy Conference (Lane keynote)
events.why_it_matters: Only ECB communication cluster inside this window before the Oct 28–29 meeting; markets are roughly 40–60% priced for another 25bp to 2.75% after the Sept 10 hike to 2.50%.
events.what_to_watch: Lane on energy/HICP pass-through and any pushback on 'live' October hike odds.

events.title: Graham Act 30-day secondary-tariff designation clock
events.why_it_matters: H.R. 5334 is law: USTR must identify top buyers of Russian oil/gas (China/India expected) and the President may impose up to 100% secondary tariffs within ~30 days — a live tariff gun sitting on the Xi table.
events.what_to_watch: Any USTR list, waiver language for China around the summit, and Indian diplomatic pushback.

events.title: Warsh Fed 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00% with hawkish SEP
events.why_it_matters: First Warsh hike, 12-0; median 2026 dots at 4.1% imply at least one more 25bp as gasoline/Hormuz inflation stays sticky and 10y yields have printed above 5%.
events.what_to_watch: PCE and NFP as the only data that can still reprice the extra hike before Oct 27–28.

events.title: BoJ hikes 25bp to 1.25% (31-year high)
events.why_it_matters: 7–2 hike one session after the Warsh Fed completes G3 tightening; Ueda called it a 'new phase' with oil-import inflation the swing factor.
events.what_to_watch: Carry-trade residual after the Sept 24 effective date and Takaichi–BoJ tension.

events.title: ECB hikes 25bp; deposit rate 2.50%
events.why_it_matters: Second 2026 hike, driven by Middle East energy inflation; staff see 2026 HICP at 3.0% and October is a live meeting.
events.what_to_watch: Euro-area energy/HICP prints and Lagarde/Lane tone at the Oct 5–6 conference.

events.title: Graham Russia/Iran Act signed (secondary-tariff authority)
events.why_it_matters: Codifies expanded Russia/Iran sanctions plus up to 100% secondary tariffs on top purchasers of Russian oil/gas and up to 500% duties on Russian goods.
events.what_to_watch: Implementation list and any China waiver tied to Sept 24.

events.title: China August activity: IP +5.2%, retail +0.4%, FAI −7.2%
events.why_it_matters: Export/high-tech supply is still running (high-tech IP +16.7%) while domestic demand and property (dev. investment −19.9% YTD) are in a deepening slump — the imbalance Xi brings to Washington.
events.what_to_watch: Whether summit optics produce any consumption/property support, or just more export-led growth.

events.title: Bessent–He Lifeng pre-summit talks (New York)
events.why_it_matters: Eight-hour Treasury–Vice Premier session was called 'very successful' and teed up a US–China AI dialogue plus tariff/rare-earth working groups for Sept 24.
events.what_to_watch: Whether those working groups actually produce text at the summit.

events.title: PBOC holds LPR 16th month (3.00%/3.50%)
events.why_it_matters: Unanimous hold confirms Beijing will not offset G3 hikes with a big easing even as FAI and consumption wilt into the Trump–Xi meeting.
events.what_to_watch: Any post-summit RRR/LPR surprise if talks go badly.

events.title: Google ad-tech remedies (no breakup) unsealed
events.why_it_matters: Judge Brinkema rejected a DOJ AdX breakup (Sept 2) and on Sept 16 imposed six-year behavioral remedies plus a compliance monitor — another Big Tech case that stopped short of structural relief.
events.what_to_watch: Oct 2 final-judgment text.

events.title: SEC 5-year innovation exemption for tokenized NMS stocks
events.why_it_matters: Temporary conditional relief lets permissioned on-chain venues trade tokenized NMS stocks for five years — a structural plus for crypto-market-structure and custody names, not a broad-market mover.
events.what_to_watch: Which incumbents file as TSVs and any issuer opt-outs.

events.title: US housing crack vs August retail-sales rebound
events.why_it_matters: Existing-home sales fell to 3.98m (4.9 months' supply, highest since 2015) and housing starts −2.6%, while advance retail sales jumped +1.2% and control-group +1.4% — split-screen into PCE/NFP.
events.what_to_watch: Sept 24 new-home sales and whether the retail bounce was gasoline/price or real volumes.

events.title: FCC waives 25% cap for Paramount–WBD Gulf funding
events.why_it_matters: Media Bureau allowed up to 49.5% non-voting foreign equity (Saudi PIF, QIA, Abu Dhabi) in the ~$110bn Paramount–Warner Bros. Discovery deal, removing a broadcast-license blocker but not state AG suits.
events.what_to_watch: Remaining state antitrust cases and any closing timeline slip.

events.title: South Korea early-September chip export boom
events.why_it_matters: Sept 1–20 exports ~$71.4bn (+78% y/y), semiconductors +259%, confirming AI-memory demand into Micron and the Trump–Xi tech agenda.
events.what_to_watch: Full-month trade (early October) and any summit export-control language that would cut the boom.

events.title: SEMICON India 2026 (Modi Semicon 2.0)
events.why_it_matters: New Delhi showcased India's subsidy/job push as a China-plus-one fab destination just as US–China AI/export-control talks peak.
events.what_to_watch: Follow-through capex announcements, not the conference itself.

top_risks: Hormuz tanker war keeps Brent ≥$100 and feeds another Warsh 25bp plus ECB/BoJ residual tightening.
Trump–Xi breakdown on Taiwan's $14bn arms package or rare earths, collapsing the Busan-truce extension into November.
Graham Act secondary tariffs on China/India collide with the summit and re-open a goods-trade shock.
Hot August PCE (Sept 30) and/or strong Oct 2 NFP lock in the SEP's extra 2026 hike with 10y already >5%.
BoJ 1.25% effective Sept 24 plus oil-import stress triggers a yen-carry unwind into month-end.
top_opportunities: Trump–Xi delivers a '30-by-30' tariff cut, AI dialogue, and Busan-truce extension — risk-on for China-sensitive cyclicals and tech hardware.
UNGA energy truce (Ukraine–Russia and/or Hormuz corridor language) that bleeds the diesel/oil war premium.
Soft PCE after NIPA revisions lets markets fade the hawkish SEP into October FOMC.
Micron/Korea chip data confirm AI-memory boom even if China domestic demand stays weak.
Costco/Nike prints that validate the August retail rebound as volumes, not just gasoline prices.
summary: The two-way overlay is unchanged and now compressed into 48 hours: Thursday's Trump–Xi summit (tariff cuts/AI vs Taiwan arms and the Graham secondary-tariff clock) against a still-unresolved Hormuz tanker war with Brent ~$101–102. G3 tightening is done for this window (Warsh 3.75–4.00%, BoJ 1.25% effective Sept 24, ECB 2.50%), so the data that can still reprice the path are Aug PCE (Sept 30) and Oct 2 NFP, while US housing is already cracking even as nominal retail sales rebounded +1.2%.
